finding.claim: purge handler performs no authorization: the checkPerm(u, "admin") result is discarded, so any caller reaching purge with a *User in context can invoke the global destructive purgeAll().
finding.source: Request reaching the purge handler with a *User in context (minimum: authenticated user; auth middleware not in repo).

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the user from request context.
checkPerm(u, "admin") evaluated but boolean return discarded; no gate.

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) lookup is correct but its result is ignored at the call site; mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is not used on this path (rotateKeys uses it correctly at lines 33-35); route-level authorization and auth middleware are not present in the repo and could not be verified. Severity HIGH (authenticated low-privilege reach, global impact); would be CRITICAL if the route is confirmed unauthenticated. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm at handlers.go:26 is a bare call whose bool return is discarded, so it is not effective. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is not called on the purge path (it is used correctly in rotateKeys at handlers.go:33). No route registration or auth middleware for purge exists in the repo; any upstream gate is unverified.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's result, handlers.go:27 calls purgeAll() unconditionally, and nothing in the repo gates it, so any caller that reaches purge with a *User in context (userFrom at handlers.go:25) can trigger it. Severity depends on the unseen router: if upstream middleware enforces admin, the handler-level defect is still real but the reachable attacker is narrower.

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked type assertion, so a request with no *User in context panics. Hardening issue, not a bypass; net/http recovers handler panics per request.
finding.source: Request reaching a handler with no user in context (missing or skipped auth middleware).

trace.note: r.Context().Value(userKey{}).(*User) panics when the value is absent or nil.
purge calls userFrom before any check, so it inherits the panic.
rotateKeys calls userFrom before mustPerm, so it inherits the panic.

finding.guards_checked: No comma-ok check; no nil guard in userFrom. Auth middleware not in repo. Severity LOW (hardening, defense-in-depth; no demonstrated bypass).

verdict.guard_found: none. No comma-ok or nil check in userFrom (handlers.go:40). The only nearby guards are mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22), which is called after userFrom and never reached on a panic, and checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14), which purge (handlers.go:26) calls but discards. Auth middleware is not in the repo, so whether a request can reach these handlers with no user in context is unknown.
verdict.reason: The panic is real: handlers.go:40 does an unchecked `.(*User)` assertion, and purge (handlers.go:25) and rotateKeys (handlers.go:32, not 33 as the trace says) both call it first. The candidate's LOW hardening framing holds, since net/http recovers handler panics, and reachability depends on middleware outside the repo. Separately, handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool, so purge has no admin check at all. That is a real authorization gap the candidate did not report, and it should be filed on its own.
